session.context:
pqac-1106eb9b: The excerpt describes a 2022 BMC Medical Education study on sustainable healthcare teaching in a London UK medical school. It used an anonymous survey circulated to 851 clinical-year medical students and students intercalating after at least one clinical year; 163 responded. The survey covered environmental impact, current teaching, and future teaching of education for sustainable healthcare (ESH). Results showed 93% saw climate change as a concern, only 1.8% had been formally taught ESH, and 89% wanted more ESH. However, the excerpt does not mention barriers to embedding ESD in UK universities, nor does it describe specific statistical analyses used for that purpose.
From Dhruv Gupta, Lahvanya Shantharam, and Bridget MacDonald. Sustainable healthcare in medical education: survey of the student perspectives at a uk medical school. BMC Medical Education, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-022-03737-5, doi:10.1186/s12909-022-03737-5.

pqac-090526b2: This excerpt describes a cross-sectional anonymous survey of medical students at a single London university. The abstract reports descriptive results only and does not mention statistical tests.
